newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise as Japan rate fears fade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs rise as Japan rate fears fade.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures gained ground on Wednesday as fears of a near-term change in the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s monetary policy faded.

The BOJ's inaction during its morning money market operation left an estimated surplus of 110 billion yen, confirming an accomodative stance and dampening fears of a potential change in policy after the Federal Reserve hiked U.S. rates by 25 basis points on Tuesday.
"At this moment, there's no clear change in stance. People know interest rates will tend to stay higher as we head for the year end," said a Japanese bank dealer.

He said fund demand for the financial year end on March 31 would place upward pressure on money market rates and players were more likely to try and discern a trend in policy after the BOJ's quarterly business sentiment survey on April 2.
December Euroyen is likely to keep to a 98.96-99.12 range in the meantime, he said. It was quoted at 99.04 at 1120 GMT after hitting a high of 99.08 against its IMM close at 98.94.

Dealers said comments by BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita that the central bank would continue to guide key money market rates below the discount rate on average reinforced the perception that the central bank's easy policy remained intact.
June JGBs settled at 125.88 against their previous 125.37 after hitting a high of 125.95.
Eurodollar futures remained sluggish after the U.S. rate hike as players had positioned themselves ahead of the move.

"The market should move sideways ahead of next week's big figures but the direction is more to the downside," said the dealer. "No matter what the technicals say, the topside looks limited because there has been a change in policy."
He said the market was already pricing in another 25 basis point hike by the Fed and added that 93.75 represented a crucial support level for September Eurodollars.
They ended unchanged against their IMM close at 93.780 on volume of 10,585 lots.
